$comment: Advisories against production dependencies that have no patched release, with the reasoning that lets this release ship anyway.
The release gate reads this file: a critical or high advisory that is neither fixed nor listed here fails the build, and so does an entry whose reviewBy date has passed.
An entry is a dated decision, not a permanent exemption. When reviewBy arrives the gate goes red again and the call surface has to be re-checked against the code as it is then.
Record the advisory id, never a count. npm reports one advisory once per node of the dependency path, so the same finding can look like six.

accepted.title: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
accepted.noFixExists: 3.0.3 is both the latest published version and inside the vulnerable range, so there is no version to upgrade to.
callSurface: No file under app/, lib/, db/, client/, runner/, worker/, scripts/ or components/ imports braces, micromatch, fast-glob or either vite plugin.
None of the five packages appears anywhere in dist/server or dist/client, so the built production artifact does not contain them.
The glob patterns reaching this matcher come from Vite plugin configuration authored in this repository, during a build. Nothing on a request path supplies them.
accepted.mitigation: The advisory needs attacker-controlled brace patterns. A build runs on a machine the operator already controls, with patterns from this repository, so the exposure is to a developer's own build rather than to a deployment. No runtime mitigation is required because the code is not present at runtime.
